purpose.description: What the system is for and who uses it; empty when no fact states it.

id.description: The capability's record id, which names its payload file.

purpose.description: What the capability offers, in one or two sentences.

screens.description: How many screens its entry points are grouped into.

actions.description: How many entry points it has.

rules.description: How many rules are decided in code it reaches.

items.description: One capability and the file that holds its payload.

capabilities.description: Every capability of the system, each with the record id that names its payload file.

scope.description: What the place is, in one sentence: its kind, its name and what it is for.

inside.description: For a place that is a map (the system, an area, a capability, a screen): what lies inside it, one line each. Capped, with the count left out in `insideNotShown`; empty for a place with nothing inside it.

insideNotShown.description: How many lines were left out of `inside`.

insideLabel.description: What `inside` lists, as a heading; empty when `inside` is empty.

lookFirst.description: Where to look first, as pointers and never a dump: the place the work starts as `file:line`, then the files the code is in with its own first and the shared ones after, the most widely shared first. Capped, with the count left out in `lookFirstNotShown`.

lookFirstNotShown.description: How many pointers were left out of `lookFirst`.

layers.description: For a screen: the layers it uses, one line each with what the layer does, `file:line` and how many of the screen's rules it decides, after where to look first; empty for any other place.

saves.description: The kinds of data the place's code saves, by name.

reads.description: The kinds of data the place's code reads, by name.

rules.description: The first rules decided there, each as its sentence with `file:line`; the rest are counted in `rulesNotShown`.

rulesNotShown.description: How many rules were left out of `rules`.

rulesTotal.description: How many rules are decided in the place's code, all told.

unconfirmed.description: What the code does not settle, as the capability's open points: what is assumed, and what would change if it is wrong. Capped.

notFollowed.description: The links in the place's code that reach nothing the code shows, each with what the code does show of where it goes. Capped.

commit.description: The commit the analysis describes, or a statement that it was not recorded.

text.description: The same context as plain text, compiled once by the analysis so every medium copies the same words. It has the lines in a fixed order, an `Ask:` line left for the reader to fill, and contains no record ids.

context.description: What a tool that reads code needs to continue from one place and no other: a map with pointers, capped, with a count of what was left out, in a fixed order. Every place has one, from the whole system down to a single rule.

items.description: One area, the group of capabilities a person names first.

areas.description: The areas of the system; none when the briefing found none.

role.description: What the layer does at the system's boundary.

purpose.description: What the layer does for the system, as the layer record states it.

group.description: The group it is read under: ui, api, data, batch, mixed or logic.

product.description: Whether the layer is the product: false when half or more of its blocks lie in tooling or tests parts, or when it is build or install scripts.

key.description: The screen's address: the path of its page file without the extension, with the folders every page shares left off.

name.description: The screen's name as the people using it say it; its page file's name when no one named it.

purpose.description: What a person does there, in one sentence; empty when no one named it.

files.description: The files its actions start in: its markup, its code-behind class and its browser scripts.

capabilities.description: The record ids of the capabilities that hold actions of this screen.

actionIds.description: The record ids of its actions, which a person starts, across capabilities.

actions.description: How many actions the screen holds, across capabilities.

rules.description: How many distinct rules its actions reach, across capabilities.

actions.description: How many of the screen's actions pass through the layer, as their paths show.

rules.description: How many of the screen's distinct rules are decided in the layer; a rule is counted once, under the one layer that decides it.

sharedRules.description: How many of those rules are reached by more than one of the screen's actions.

items.description: One layer a screen touches: the layers its actions pass through and the layers that decide the rules its actions reach, in flow order (person-facing first, store last).

layersTouched.description: The layers the screen touches merged across its capabilities, each action and rule counted once.

items.description: One screen a person uses, merged across the capabilities that hold its actions.

screens.description: Every screen a person uses, merged by page across capabilities, so a page is one screen however many capabilities its actions serve. Actions that other systems or a schedule start belong to no screen.

from.description: The layer a link leaves, by record id.

to.description: The layer a link reaches, by record id.

kind.description: How the link reaches: call, renders, reads, saves, request or dispatches.

links.description: How many links of that kind between the two layers.

items.description: The links of one kind from one layer to another.

edges.description: The links between layers; links into shapes of data reach no block and are not counted.

otherSystem.description: Entry points another system or the runtime starts.

entries.description: How many entry points each kind of starter has, across the system.

name.description: What it is, in plain words.

kind.description: What kind of thing outside the code it is; groups external systems on pages. A `library` is code with no source here: a call into it names the operation as its resource, never data, and the flow is not followed further (P12.3).

links.description: How many links of the product's code reach it.

layer.description: The layer's record id; empty when no layer holds the block.

access.description: How the layer reaches it: call, reads, saves, renders or request.

links.description: How many links of that kind.

reach.description: The layers that reach it, and how.

externals.description: What the code reaches outside itself, most reached first; libraries are not listed.

unresolvedLinks.description: Links in the whole system that reach nothing the code shows.

unattributedBlocks.description: Blocks no entry point reaches, so no capability has them.

gaps.description: What the analysis could not follow in the whole system.
